data.long_meaning: In Islamic context, the name Furqan means a distinction, difference, or division between right and wrong. The Quran refers to this term as ‘Al-Furqan’ (The Criterion), which distinguishes truth from falsehood and guides people towards the right path. The name Furqau carries the meaning “Division, Separation” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Furqau usually hope their child will grow to embody division, separation and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Qutaybah records the existence of a prominent scholar and jurist named Furqan ibn Iyad al-Basri in his book 'Al-Imamah wa al-Siyasah'. He lived during the early Abbasid Caliphate (750-868 CE) and was known for his scholarship in Hadith and Fiqh.

Al-Maqrizi in his book 'Al-Khutabat al-Saniyah' mentions Furqan ibn al-A'raj as the name of the fifth Fatimid caliph, who ruled from 1036 to 1045 CE during the Fatimid Caliphate. He succeeded his father, Al-Mustansir Billah, and was known for his military conquests and his patronage of the sciences and arts.
